glossary.definition: (A) "Sexual conduct" means vaginal intercourse between a male and female; anal intercourse, fellatio, and cunnilingus between persons regardless of sex; and, without privilege to do so, the insertion, however slight, of any part of the body or any instrument, apparatus, or other object into the vaginal or anal opening of another. Penetration, however slight, is sufficient to complete vaginal or anal intercourse.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 2907.01 to 2907.38 and 2917.211 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (B) "Sexual contact" means any touching of an erogenous zone of another, including without limitation the thigh, genitals, buttock, pubic region, or, if the person is a female, a breast, for the purpose of sexually arousing or gratifying either person.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 2907.01 to 2907.38 and 2917.211 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (C) "Sexual activity" means sexual conduct or sexual contact, or both.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 2907.01 to 2907.38 and 2917.211 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (D) "Prostitute" means a male or female who promiscuously engages in sexual activity for hire, regardless of whether the hire is paid to the prostitute or to another.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 2907.01 to 2907.38 and 2917.211 of the Revised Code:
As used in sections 2907.01 to 2907.38 and 2917.211 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (G) "Sexual excitement" means the condition of human male or female genitals when in a state of sexual stimulation or arousal.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 2907.01 to 2907.38 and 2917.211 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (H) "Nudity" means the showing, representation, or depiction of human male or female genitals, pubic area, or buttocks with less than a full, opaque covering, or of a female breast with less than a full, opaque covering of any portion thereof below the top of the nipple, or of covered male genitals in a discernibly turgid state.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 2907.01 to 2907.38 and 2917.211 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (I) "Juvenile" means an unmarried person under the age of eighteen.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 2907.01 to 2907.38 and 2917.211 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (J) "Material" means any book, magazine, newspaper, pamphlet, poster, print, picture, figure, image, description, motion picture film, phonographic record, or tape, or other tangible thing capable of arousing interest through sight, sound, or touch and includes an image or text appearing on a computer monitor, television screen, liquid crystal display, or similar display device or an image or text recorded on a computer hard disk, computer floppy disk, compact disk, magnetic tape, or similar data storage device.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 2907.01 to 2907.38 and 2917.211 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (K) "Performance" means any motion picture, preview, trailer, play, show, skit, dance, or other exhibition performed before an audience.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 2907.01 to 2907.38 and 2917.211 of the Revised Code:
As used in sections 2907.01 to 2907.38 and 2917.211 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (M) "Minor" means a person under the age of eighteen.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 2907.01 to 2907.38 and 2917.211 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (N) "Mental health client or patient" has the same meaning as in section 2305.51 of the Revised Code.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 2907.01 to 2907.38 and 2917.211 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (O) "Mental health professional" has the same meaning as in section 2305.115 of the Revised Code.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 2907.01 to 2907.38 and 2917.211 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (P) "Sado-masochistic abuse" means flagellation or torture by or upon a person or the condition of being fettered, bound, or otherwise physically restrained.
glossary.scope: As used in sections 2907.01 to 2907.38 and 2917.211 of the Revised Code:

glossary.definition: (Q) "Place where a person has a reasonable expectation of privacy" means a place where a reasonable person would believe that the person could fully disrobe in private.
glossary.normalized: place where a person has a reasonable expectation of privacy

glossary.definition: (R) "Private area" means the genitals, pubic area, buttocks, or female breast below the top of the areola, where nude or covered by an undergarment.
